question: Assume today is 2026-09-06. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park in September 2026, as it will be reported in the National Park Service's official monthly visitation statistics.

target.what: Recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park as reported in the National Park Service's official monthly visitation statistics (NPS Monthly Public Use Report). A recreation visit is one person entering the park for recreational purposes; the same person entering multiple times on separate occasion
target.publisher: National Park Service (NPS), Public Use Statistics Office / Social Science Program
target.cadence: Monthly, typically published 4-8 weeks after the end of the month
target.caveats: The target period is future relative to the 2026-09-06 cutoff, so no September 2026 data exist yet. The estimate must be built from historical seasonal patterns, recent 2026 monthly data (through July or August 2026 if published before the cutoff), and any available signals about park access, weathe

candidates.hypothesis: September recreation visits in recent years (2015-2025) show a stable seasonal pattern and trend that can be extrapolated to 2026, adjusted for any known shocks. The ratio of September visits to the preceding July/August peak or to the annual total provides a base rate.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly recreation visit counts for Yellowstone National Park for September 2015-2025, and for July and August 2015-2025. Also annual totals for 2015-2025. Minimum evidence: September values for at least the last 5 years and the corresponding July/August values to compute seasonal shares.
search_hints: Yellowstone National Park monthly visitation statistics September 2025
NPS public use statistics Yellowstone monthly recreation visits

candidates.perspective: NPS year-to-date and recent monthly data for 2026
candidates.hypothesis: Year-to-date 2026 visitation through July or August, combined with the historical share of September in the annual total, yields an estimate for September 2026. If 2026 YTD is above/below recent years, September may follow a similar deviation.
candidates.data_to_find: Yellowstone recreation visits for January-August 2026 (or through the latest month published before 2026-09-06), and the same YTD periods for 2023-2025. Also the historical share of September visits relative to January-September or annual totals. Minimum evidence: 2026 YTD total and at least 3 years of comparable YTD and September data.
search_hints: NPS Yellowstone 2026 monthly public use report

candidates.hypothesis: Recreation visits can be estimated from vehicle entries at park entrances multiplied by average occupancy, adjusted for non-recreation entries and seasonality. September vehicle counts and occupancy rates may be available from traffic counters or entrance station data.
candidates.data_to_find: Vehicle entry counts at Yellowstone entrances for September in recent years, and average persons per vehicle for September. If unavailable, use national park average occupancy (e.g., 2.5-3.0) and adjust for Yellowstone's specific patterns. Minimum evidence: at least one recent September vehicle count and an occupancy estimate.
search_hints: Yellowstone average occupancy per vehicle visitation

candidates.perspective: Lodging, campground, and gateway community occupancy
candidates.hypothesis: September visitation is constrained by available lodging and campground capacity and their occupancy rates. Total overnight stays plus day-use visits can be estimated from accommodation capacity and utilization, then converted to recreation visits using average length of stay and day-trip ratios.
candidates.data_to_find: Yellowstone lodging and campground capacity (number of rooms/sites), September occupancy rates for 2023-2025, average length of stay, and proportion of visitors staying overnight vs. day trips. Minimum evidence: September occupancy for at least one recent year and capacity figures.

candidates.perspective: Park closures, weather, and access restrictions
candidates.hypothesis: Any closures or access restrictions in September 2026 (e.g., road closures, wildfires, government shutdown, flood recovery) would reduce visitation relative to the historical pattern. Conversely, a major anniversary or promotion could increase it. The direction and magnitude of the shock must be estimated from news and official announcements.
candidates.data_to_find: News of Yellowstone closures, road conditions, wildfire activity, or special events for September 2026 (as known by 2026-09-06). Also historical examples of September closures (e.g., 2022 flood) and their impact on monthly visitation. Minimum evidence: any official NPS announcement about September 2026 access.

candidates.perspective: Seasonal share of September in annual visitation
candidates.hypothesis: The share of annual recreation visits occurring in September is relatively stable across years (e.g., 10-12%). Multiplying a forecast of 2026 annual visitation by this share gives a September estimate. Annual visitation can be forecast from 2026 YTD and historical growth rates.
candidates.data_to_find: September share of annual recreation visits for Yellowstone for 2015-2025, and a forecast of 2026 annual visitation (from NPS, tourism forecasts, or extrapolation of YTD). Minimum evidence: September shares for at least 5 years and a 2026 annual forecast or YTD data.

candidates.perspective: Search and social media interest in Yellowstone
candidates.hypothesis: Google Trends or social media mentions for Yellowstone in September 2026 may correlate with visitation, but the relationship is noisy and not a direct conversion. Use only as a directional check if other routes are uncertain.
candidates.data_to_find: Google Trends search interest for 'Yellowstone National Park' for September 2026 (if available before cutoff) and historical correlation with monthly visitation. Minimum evidence: historical correlation coefficient between search interest and visitation for September months.
search_hints: Google Trends Yellowstone National Park September
Yellowstone social media mentions September visitation correlation

candidates.perspective: Published tourism forecasts and prediction markets
candidates.hypothesis: Any published forecast for Yellowstone 2026 visitation or prediction market on September 2026 visitation could provide a direct estimate or a range. These may incorporate expert judgment and current conditions.
candidates.data_to_find: Tourism forecasts for Yellowstone 2026 (e.g., from NPS, University of Montana, or travel industry), and any prediction market contracts on Yellowstone visitation. Minimum evidence: at least one credible forecast or market price.

a1.role: September share of annual Yellowstone recreation visits

methods.rationale: Seasonal-share decomposition: September 2026 recreation visits = forecast 2026 annual recreation visits times the historical September share. This is the only executable route with the currently kept evidence. It requires two assumptions because no 2026 monthly or annual Yellowstone data and no historical September share are available in the kept points. The main failure modes are a 2026 annual level outside the assumed range and a September share shifted by weather, closures, or reporting changes. The Grand Teton June 2026 point (p25) is a weak regional analogue and is not used numerically.

assumptions.name: September share of annual Yellowstone recreation visits
assumptions.rationale: Historical NPS monthly patterns for Yellowstone typically place September in the high-single-digit to low-double-digit percentage range of annual recreation visits. The range is widened to reflect year-to-year variation, weather, and access shocks. This is a dimensionless share, not the target level.
assumptions.applies_when: Used only to convert a forecast or observed 2026 annual Yellowstone recreation visit total into a September 2026 estimate under normal access conditions.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 has major closures or that recent September shares have shifted outside the 8-14% range.

assumptions.name: 2026 annual Yellowstone recreation visits
assumptions.rationale: No 2026 annual total is available at the cutoff. The value is a broad prior centered near recent Yellowstone annual visitation levels, with uncertainty reflecting incomplete 2026 data and possible access or demand shocks. It is not the target September level.
assumptions.applies_when: Used only as a forecast annual total for 2026 to be multiplied by the September share.
assumptions.falsified_by: Published 2026 YTD or annual Yellowstone visitation data showing a level outside the stated range.

assessment.note: All are 2026 Yellowstone road-opening/closure schedule entries from the same NPS page (snapshot 2026-09-06). They jointly establish that the park's road network is open through September 2026: West Entrance-Madison, Madison-Old Faithful, Madison-Norris, Mammoth-Norris, Norris-Canyon open Apr 17-Oct 31; East Entrance-Fishing Bridge and Canyon-Bridge Bay open May 1-Oct 31; South Entrance-West Thumb, West Thumb-Old Faithful, West Thumb-Lake Village, Tower-Roosevelt-Tower Fall open May 8-Oct 31. Only Dunraven Pass (Canyon-Tower Fall) and the Beartooth/Chief Joseph byways close Oct 12, i.e. after the target month. This is a shared-source cluster, not independent confirmation, but it is the key evidence that no scheduled September access restriction exists.

Fire-activity page last updated July 21, 2026, with no indication of a large active fire. Weak, dated signal; it does not establish September 2026 fire conditions, so it can only support the assumption that no major fire-driven closure is known as of the cutoff.

Grand Teton June 2026 visitors (798,286) and May 2026 US inflation (4.2%) come from the same Wyoming Public Media snapshot. They are regional/economic context for the Greater Yellowstone area, not Yellowstone recreation visits and not a September 2026 quantity; they cannot be substituted into a Yellowstone September formula.

decisions.reason: Different park (Grand Teton) and different month (June 2026); no defensible conversion to Yellowstone September 2026 recreation visits.
Macroeconomic inflation rate for May 2026; no established quantitative bridge to Yellowstone September visitation and not a visit count.
A page-update date, not a fire-impact measurement; it carries no numeric information usable in a formula and is superseded by the road-schedule evidence for September access.

a2.role: Average September recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park, 2019-2025

methods.rationale: Seasonal-transfer route: the historical September base (a2) times a 2026 transfer factor (a1). The road schedule (p37-p41) confirms full September access, so the main uncertainty is demand, not access. Shared dependency: all road points come from one NPS page, so they confirm access but not visitation level. Failure mode: if a September 2026 shock occurs after the cutoff, the transfer factor is wrong; if 2026 YTD data later show a large deviation, the base should be revised.

assumptions.name: September 2026 Yellowstone recreation visits as a multiple of the 2019-2025 September average
assumptions.rationale: No 2026 monthly Yellowstone data are available at the cutoff, so the level must be transferred from the historical September base. The road schedule (p37-p41) shows the park fully open through September 2026, and no September 2026 closure, wildfire, or shutdown is documented as of 2026-09-06. The range allows for post-2022 flood-recovery normalisation, inflation/economic drag (p26 is only weak context), and normal weather variability; it is deliberately wide because the transfer is unobserved.
assumptions.applies_when: The park remains open through September 2026 with no major new closure, wildfire, or government shutdown, and 2026 demand is broadly in line with the recent 2019-2025 September pattern.
assumptions.falsified_by: A September 2026 road closure, wildfire evacuation, government shutdown, or credible 2026 YTD data showing a large deviation from the recent September base.

assumptions.name: Average September recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park, 2019-2025
assumptions.rationale: The historical September level is the base for the seasonal-transfer route. No kept data point supplies a Yellowstone September count, so this level must be assumed. The value reflects the typical recent September magnitude (roughly 0.6-0.8 million visits in recent years, with 2022 depressed by the June flood and 2020-2021 affected by COVID), and the range spans the plausible multi-year average.
assumptions.applies_when: Used as the historical September base for transferring to September 2026 under the assumption that the 2019-2025 average is a reasonable anchor for the current seasonal level.
assumptions.falsified_by: Publication of actual Yellowstone September monthly counts for 2019-2025 showing the average outside this range.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

ablation.rule: exclude points from own_history directions and points whose name contains a target entity anchor and whose name or unit shares a stem with the target unit (triangulate/agent/ablation.py)
residual_risks: Own values named by an alias or abbreviation, or with no entity in the point name, are not excluded.

The rule over-excludes on purpose: any point naming the target entity together with the target quantity (for example a survey of the target's visitors) is excluded, even when it is not a value of the target itself.
The model's own memory of the target's history is not removed: it can still shape the plan, the judge's choices and assumption values.
The searcher and the extractor still see pages that contain own values; only the judge's table is filtered.
